fields.v: Shayanfar, R., Gallaba, K., Hassan, A. E. (2026). Choosing Coding-Agent Benchmarks for Practice: Lessons from Task Demands and Agent Behaviour. arXiv:2609.01271v2 [cs.SE], 27 Oct 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2609.01271v2 [cs.SE] (IEEE conference format); no venue stated
Queen's University, Kingston, Canada (academia; two authors); Centre for Software Excellence, Huawei Canada (industry; one author)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Evaluates — Spread-Novelty-Centrality (SNC) profile for characterising benchmark tasks by their gold patches, applied to 2,487 tasks from five public benchmarks and 14,922 runs of six agent configurations (patch scope, exploration, association with resolution); lessons and a local workflow for practitioners

No SDD approach. Agent configurations evaluated: Claude Code 2.1.108 with Claude Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.6; Qwen Code 0.14.4 with Qwen 3.5 9B, 27B, 397B-A17B. Evaluation method: SNC profile (seven indicators) and footprint ratios; proposed four-step local evaluation workflow

N/A for the agents (benchmark problem statements only, with or without hints such as signatures and docstrings). Proposed workflow retains per historical change: request, base commit, accepted patch, available tests, information developers had; per attempt: model, scaffold, instructions, tools, limits, final patch, outcome, trajectory

Study: compute SNC indicators on gold patches (RQ1) -> run six configurations via Harbor -> compare agent patch and exploration with gold patch for Opus-resolved tasks (RQ2) -> contrast resolved vs unresolved runs (RQ3). Proposed local workflow: define the work to represent -> compare local task profile with candidate benchmarks -> evaluate the complete configuration and retain evidence -> inspect deviations before changing the workflow
None in the agent runs. Proposed workflow: reviewers inspect unusually small or large patches (resolved and unresolved) and check scope deviations before setting scope policies

fields.why: Patch scope ratios (agent vs gold files, lines, callables) and the gold-patch SNC indicators describe size and location of changes, not maintainability or technical debt; the authors say resolved patches are not shown equivalent in maintainability (p. 5), smaller patches are not quality goals (p. 6) and patch size does not measure review effort (p. 9). Another reader could still treat patch scope vs gold as an internal-quality proxy.

fields.v: Automatic: Harbor harness test outcomes, agent patches and trajectories; static analysis of gold and agent patches, import graphs and commit history (Radon); LLM classification of problem statements

Harbor harness, Docker, default timeouts and decoding; one run per task. Success criterion per run: benchmark tests accept the patch. No quality or cost success criterion for a configuration stated by the authors. Cramer's V per configuration from Table II (rebuilt row-wise): SNC indicators range; behaviour ratios files / lines / callables / explore. (1) Claude Code 2.1.108 + Claude Haiku 4.5: resolution count not reported; SNC V 0.21-0.35; behaviour V .38 / .33 / .40 / .13; resolved runs frequently exceed 2x gold files and lines; file-parity share of resolved runs 0.17, exploration parity 0.09. (2) Claude Code + Claude Sonnet 4.6: count not reported; SNC V 0.15-0.23; behaviour V .23 / .10 / .16 / .12; file-parity share 0.41. (3) Claude Code + Claude Opus 4.6: resolves 1,083 of 2,487 tasks; SNC V 0.17-0.28; behaviour V .23 / .15 / .18 / .15; file-parity share 0.54, exploration parity 0.34; patches larger than gold on FeatBench, smaller on FeatureBench, near parity elsewhere. (4) Qwen Code 0.14.4 + Qwen 3.5 9B: SNC V 0.15-0.26; behaviour V .24 / .13 / .23 / .02 (n.s.). (5) + Qwen 3.5 27B: SNC V 0.14-0.23; behaviour V .24 / .18 / .21 / .03 (n.s.). (6) + Qwen 3.5 397B-A17B: SNC V 0.19-0.30; behaviour V .31 / .21 / .26 / .07. Qwen (4)-(6): counts not reported; about 0.6-0.7 of resolved runs above 2x gold file count, about 0.2 near parity; about 0.8 above 2x in exploration. Quality verdict and cost verdict for every configuration: no criterion stated by the authors

Observational. Tasks: 2,487 from five public benchmarks. Configurations: two families (Claude Code + Claude, Qwen Code + Qwen) x three model sizes; no baseline. Held constant: Harbor harness, Docker environments, default task timeouts, default decoding; scaffolds differ across families. Acceptance tests: benchmarks' prescribed tests. Repetitions: one run per task and configuration. Human intervention: none. Statistics: Scott-Knott ESD (alpha 0.05, |d| >= 0.2), chi-square with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, Cramer's V. Runs 14 April - 2 June 2026

Benchmarks: every pair differs on at least two SNC axes, including same-label pairs. Configurations: resolved runs concentrate on lower Spread and Centrality in both families (all 42 indicator-configuration associations significant, V 0.14-0.35); larger Claude configurations more often match gold scope (file parity 0.17 / 0.41 / 0.54), Qwen resolved runs mostly exceed it; behaviour associations significant in 22 of 24 comparisons. Claude Opus 4.6 is the highest-performing configuration (rates not given)

SNC profile separated all benchmark pairs; exploration breadth did not separate benchmarks. Not repeatable as designed: one run per task, authors state repeated runs would be needed to quantify stochastic variation. Limitations stated: different scaffolds confound cross-family contrasts; different resolved subsets within family; observational comparisons (hints, repositories, construction rules co-vary); tasks from the same repository related and FEA-Bench dominates pooled tests; Python only

SNC profile measures properties of a reference change, not the full engineering work (omits requirement ambiguity, domain knowledge, runtime interactions); gold patch is one accepted implementation; tests may miss requirements; Python-only public tasks; findings may not persist across model or scaffold updates; local replication and practitioner assessment needed before using it for task assignment, review effort or deployment; industrial evaluation of the workflow planned; integration effort, productivity and review costs not measured

Per-configuration resolution rates are not reported (only Opus's 1,083 resolved tasks), although Lesson workflow recommends reporting attempted and resolved counts. Table II values rebuilt from pdftotext column order. FEA-Bench converted to Harbor format by the authors. Code for SNC profile and analyses at github.com/radinshayanfar/task_snc. Generative AI used for implementation and editing. No pre-registration. Programming language of tasks: Python
